answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so coordinated equivocation by k identities triggers correlated penalties scaling as O(k^2), rather than k independent fines. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the controlling escrow, with asymmetric depreciation preventing recovery through replacement accounts. Thus an attacker gains little from multiplying identities: every echo reinforces evidence, while each inlet or reef of coordination increases the cost of the swarm.
